scope: Corollary I.9 (Globalizing returned patches) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 189. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition I.6 and sampling Property 3, let 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1. A family as in Lemma I.8, with real input a = f − λ, yields an ambient patch of rank at most d∗ + P h dim Wh, with positive score after the prescribed fixed multiplicative discount of the target density. Its logarithmic inverse score, output slice costs, and complexity may include the subspace heights and later parameters, as allowed in sampling Property 3. They have polynomial bounds in that augmented log budget, rather than necessarily early bounds.
